title: mansio on main (636cc30; S3 work paused)

elements.name: Application developer / caller
elements.description: Writes and calls TypeScript handlers in the caller application.

elements.name: Platform operator
elements.description: Administers the platform with mansioctl (tenants, databases, moves, attest-dead and restore, one agent's controls) and dbtool (the S3 copies); reads or ships the request log and scrapes metrics.

elements.name: mansio Go platform
elements.description: Go-only document database platform; a database is the isolation and placement unit, and a tenant may own many databases.

elements.name: Caller application
elements.description: User application outside the server boundary; hosts the TypeScript SDK and application handlers.

elements.name: Caller process + SDK
elements.description: Application handlers and the TypeScript SDK run together here, outside the Go server.

elements.name: TypeScript SDK
elements.description: Records reads, buffers writes and derives asserts. Batches reads into one snapshot per run and guards finds with a table assert. Re-runs handlers on eligible conflicts from the state the conflict returns.

elements.name: Read cache
elements.description: Documents by id with the version they were read at. Answers a mutation's get without a round trip; never trusted: the SDK asserts every cached version before or in the commit.

elements.name: S3 — built, paused
elements.description: Implemented immutable SQLite generations and manifests. Work paused 2026-11-06 pending LiteFS; crash recovery can lose acknowledged writes.

elements.name: controld
elements.description: Control daemon: registries, database lifecycle, locator/routing, epoch authority access and signed-ticket issuing.

elements.name: edge / TLS proxy
elements.description: Separate stateless proxy; verifies tickets and routes by VM to private agentd. Refuses before reading the body (max_in_flight, agent bulkhead, breaker). No compiler or database engine.

elements.name: agentd / Go server
elements.description: Per-VM daemon and database server in one process: ticket admission, actors, local files and lifecycle RPC.

elements.name: SQLite files
elements.description: One file per database; many databases per tenant. Local WAL, request-id records and the commit sequence (_mansio_changes); database is the isolation unit.

elements.name: Placement registry
elements.description: Postgres placement and tenancy registry; CAS enforces epoch invariants. Local/test setups also have a file authority.

elements.name: Request log (JSONL)
elements.description: One JSON line per request, handler run, transaction and SQL statement, under the request's trace id. The writer drops records when its queue is full (counted) and deletes its oldest files past its size and age limits.

elements.name: Ticket admission
elements.description: Verifies signed claims offline and checks VM, database, permission and locally ACTIVE epoch. Caps in-flight work per database, tenant and VM; sheds a request that would expire in its queue.

elements.name: IR executor
elements.description: Validates document IR, dispatches actor closures and checks fingerprint and preconditions (including table asserts). Conflict answers carry seq and current state. Never runs application TypeScript.

elements.name: Document → SQL compiler
elements.description: Compiles document reads and writes to parameterized SQLite SQL inside execution.

elements.name: Bounded mailbox
elements.description: Nonblocking enqueue per database; full queues shed work and expired queued work does not run.

elements.name: Database actor
elements.description: One goroutine per database; runs closures on its connection. Each run reads one snapshot; optional read pool provides concurrent read snapshots.

elements.name: Group commit
elements.description: One write connection per actor. Batch transaction, individual write savepoints; _version and commit sequence never fall below the incarnation floor. Replies follow commit.

elements.name: Request-id registry
elements.description: Claims _mansio_requests inside the write savepoint. Commits result with mutation; retained duplicates replay without reapplying.

elements.name: Write-back — paused
elements.description: Implemented snapshots, restore and epoch-stamped manifests; the manifest seal is the incarnation behind the version floor. S3 work paused 2026-11-06 pending LiteFS; no WAL shipping.

elements.name: Structured event sink
elements.description: Nonblocking bounded queue and writer goroutine; flushes rolled JSONL, counts drops and losses, and retires its oldest files past max_total_bytes / max_age.

elements.name: Locator
elements.description: Authenticates API key; returns endpoint, epoch, generation and signed ticket. Refreshes stale placement from primary. Store loads and creates take narrow slots below the Postgres pool.

elements.name: Epoch authority
elements.description: Linearizable placement Get/CAS through Postgres. Owner changes require a higher epoch.

elements.name: Ticket signer
elements.description: Signs tenant, database, VM, epoch, principal, permissions and expiry with Ed25519.

elements.name: Lifecycle controller
elements.description: Creates, moves, suspends/resumes, drops and restores databases; records operator attest-dead. Finishes stuck flows from table scans.

elements.name: Source agentd
elements.description: Source VM role of agentd: stop admission, drain, final write-back and durable FENCED before Ack.

elements.name: Target agentd
elements.description: Target VM role of agentd: verify authority, fetch generation and stamp new epoch before admission.

2. CAS ACTIVE(source,E) to MOVING(source,E)
3. Stop admission and drain source work
4. Final write-back: immutable G and manifest at E; built, paused

documents.title: mansio Go platform: context
documents.plain: The caller runs application handlers. mansio runs Go IR execution. Operators manage lifecycle and read the request log and metrics. S3 integration is implemented but paused by Nick on 2026-11-06 pending a LiteFS decision. Existing status denotes code at the pin, not live deployment.

ste.text: The caller runs application handlers. mansio runs Go IR execution. Operators manage the lifecycle. Operators read the request log and the metrics. S3 integration is implemented but paused by Nick on 2026-11-06 pending a LiteFS decision. Existing status denotes code at the pin, not live deployment.

documents.title: Request path: caller → control plane once → data plane
documents.plain: The TypeScript SDK is a library inside the caller process. Resolve returns a route and signed ticket. Reuse the cached route until refresh or invalidation; controld is not a per-query hop. The returned endpoint may be the edge, which forwards directly to agentd. agentd is both the VM daemon and Go server. Each tenant can own many databases. S3 storage is built but paused. Agents fetch ticket public keys from controld, so tickets verify offline; the edge polls controld's VM registry for routes. Lifecycle RPC, the agent's placement connection and S3 exist in durable mode only.

documents.title: Caller process: in-process SDK and handler retries
documents.plain: The SDK records handler reads and buffered writes in the caller process. It derives preconditions, including table asserts for finds, and sends IR. A mutation's get can come from the read cache; the cached version is asserted before or in the commit, so a stale entry costs one round trip, never a commit on old data. Eligible conflicts re-run the handler in this same process from the state the conflict answer carries. Route and signed-ticket caching avoid a control-plane lookup for every query.

documents.title: agentd: admission, IR and per-database execution
documents.plain: Admission verifies the ticket and local epoch, caps in-flight work per database, tenant and VM, and sheds what would expire in its queue. The IR adapter queues a closure; an actor executes it, checking preconditions (document and table asserts) and compiling SQL. Each database has a bounded mailbox, goroutine and write connection. Writes share a batch transaction but have individual savepoints. Request-id claim, mutation and recorded result commit together; retained duplicate results replay. Each run reads one snapshot, optionally on a read pool. A conflict answer carries the current state, from which the SDK re-runs a handler; no application handler runs here. Every bounded queue reports depth, capacity and refusals on /metrics (mansio_queue_*).

documents.title: agentd: paused durability and canonical events
documents.plain: The event sink writes the request log (JSONL) through a bounded queue; drops and records lost at close are counted, so canonical does not mean lossless, and the writer retires its oldest files past its size and age limits. The separate durable host snapshots SQLite and publishes immutable generations. S3 work is IMPLEMENTED BUT PAUSED, not proposed. The acknowledgement is the local commit; the unpublished window is about 11 seconds with the defaults and unbounded while S3 is down, so acknowledged writes may be lost on crash. Version and sequence reuse after a rollback are closed by the incarnation floor. WAL shipping and LiteFS replacement are not built.

documents.title: controld: locator, signer and epoch authority
documents.plain: The locator authenticates an API key, reads placement and signs a ticket. Store loads and creates take narrow slots kept below the Postgres pool budget. The authority adapter uses Postgres CAS. The operator drives it with mansioctl, the one admin CLI (databases, vms, keys, limits, tenants). The lifecycle controller moves databases and records operator attest-dead decisions; restore then asks live target agents to claim last published generations. Attest-dead belongs to controld, not to the edge or agentd. Durable restore depends on the implemented but paused S3 path.

documents.title: Request log (JSONL) and metrics
documents.plain: agentd writes its request log: one JSON line per /v1/ops request (http), handler run, transaction (tx) and, with trace_sql, SQL statement (sql), all under the request's trace id, in <dir>/server/<date>/events-<HH>-<pid>-<seq>.jsonl. Emitting never blocks a request: a full queue drops the record, and the writer counts drops and write losses, reports drops as queue records, and deletes its oldest files past max_total_bytes and max_age. The operator reads the files in place (jq, the optional duckdb CLI) or ships them with the deployment's log collector; no log store, collector or offline analysis tool is part of the platform (ADR 0014). Health and overload are Prometheus metrics, not log records: agentd serves /metrics, /healthz, /livez and /readyz, its mansio_eventlog_* families count the request log's written, dropped and lost records and deleted files, agentd, the edge and controld export mansio_queue_* families, and deploy/prometheus/backpressure.rules.yml ships the alert rules (no Prometheus server is part of the platform).

ste.text: agentd writes a request log. The log has one JSON line for each /v1/ops request, handler run, transaction and SQL statement. Each line has the trace id of its request. The files are in <dir>/server/<date>/. agentd does not wait for the log: when the queue is full, agentd drops the record and counts it. The writer deletes the oldest files when the files are too large or too old. The operator reads the files with jq or the duckdb CLI, or sends them to a log store with a log collector. The platform does not include a log store, a log collector or an analysis tool. Metrics show health and overload: agentd serves /metrics, /healthz, /livez and /readyz. The mansio_eventlog metrics count the written, dropped and lost records. The file deploy/prometheus/backpressure.rules.yml contains the alert rules. The platform does not include a Prometheus server.

documents.title: Query: resolve once, then cached-ticket data path
documents.plain: This successful first-query scenario resolves once. Subsequent calls reuse the cached ticket, subject to TTL refresh or stale-owner invalidation. The edge is a direct data-plane proxy, not another call through controld; it and admission refuse overload before work is queued. Ticket validation occurs again in agentd. Reads asked for together travel as one request and answer at one snapshot. Compilation and SQLite execution run within the actor closure. Return steps are numbered explicitly.

documents.title: Database move: fence before epoch flip (S3 built, paused)
documents.plain: Successful graceful move in the implemented durable mode; S3 work is paused. Source and target boxes are two runtime roles of the same agentd executable, not different services. The source stops admission, drains admitted work, performs final write-back and durably records FENCED before acknowledgment. Only then may the authority flip to target at E+1. Claim checks authority, fetches G, stamps storage and persists ACTIVE before serving. A failed step leaves the move resumable; no unconditional flip after an unacknowledged fence. Attest-dead restore is a different path with an accepted loss window.

documents.title: TypeScript SDK
documents.plain: Records gets and buffered writes, derives version/existence asserts, and re-runs the handler on eligible conflicts. Reads asked for together are one request, and each run reads at one snapshot (seq). A find is guarded by a table assert (unchangedSince); find(...).unguarded() opts out. Retries follow the shared retry contract: expired is final.

documents.title: Read cache
documents.plain: In-memory LRU (1024 documents by default) of documents with the version they were read at. Only a mutation's get reads it; queries fill it. The SDK asserts the version of every cached document a handler read in the run's next request or its commit, so a stale entry costs one round trip and never a commit on old data. A conflict without current state evicts every asserted document.

documents.plain: The per-VM daemon IS the Go database server: ticket admission, actors and last-mile files; lifecycle Claim/Fence/Forget/Health. Two modes: static (local *.db files at fixed epochs; no moves) and durable (S3 virtual-actor host plus placement authority; required for moves and restore; S3 work built but paused). Not a second server behind agentd.

documents.title: Request log (JSONL)
documents.plain: The request log as agentd writes it: JSON lines with a fixed envelope (eventId, ts, level, role, pid, traceId, spanId, parentSpanId, appId, kind) and per-kind keys, redacted, never with bind values. Bounded logging can drop records and reports drops. The writer deletes its oldest files past max_total_bytes (4 GiB) or max_age (45 days) and counts what it retires. It is the record a log collector ships, not the request-path authority.

ste.text: This is the request log that agentd writes. Each line is a JSON object. Each line has the same envelope fields and the fields of its kind. The log does not contain bind values or tokens. agentd can drop records when the queue is full, and it counts the dropped records. The writer deletes the oldest files after 4 GiB or 45 days, and it counts the deleted files. A log collector can send these files to a log store.

documents.title: Ticket admission
documents.plain: Verifies signed claims offline; admits only the matching database, permissions, VM and locally ACTIVE epoch. In-flight caps per database, tenant and VM; a request that would not finish before its deadline is shed at once (503 with Retry-After) instead of queuing until it expires.

documents.title: IR executor
documents.plain: POST /v1/ops decodes IR and dispatches an actor closure. Checks fingerprint, bodies and preconditions, including table asserts (unchangedSince); runs IR, never application TypeScript. Every non-duplicate answer carries the commit sequence; a conflict answer carries seq and the current documents.

documents.title: Database actor
documents.plain: One goroutine per database. Executes closures on the database connection; optional read pool runs read snapshots.

documents.title: Group commit
documents.plain: One write connection per actor; queued writes share BEGIN IMMEDIATE / COMMIT, each with its own savepoint. A write sets _version and the commit sequence at or above the incarnation floor (manifest seal << 32), so neither repeats after a rollback; in durable mode both start at 2^32. Replies follow commit.

documents.title: Request-id registry
documents.plain: Claims _mansio_requests inside the write savepoint, records result with the write and replays retained results without reapplying. Failed writes roll back their claim.

documents.title: Write-back — paused
documents.plain: IMPLEMENTED BUT PAUSED: virtual-actor snapshots and restore use immutable S3 generations; conditional manifest publish and epoch stamp fence stale publishers. The manifest seal counts activations and is the incarnation behind the version and sequence floor. No incremental WAL shipping.

documents.title: Locator
documents.plain: Authenticates API key and resolves database owner; returns endpoint, epoch, generation and ticket. Refreshes stale routes using the primary. Resolves pass a wide gate; store loads and creates on first use take narrow gates budgeted below the Postgres pool, and a full narrow gate sheds at once.

documents.title: Epoch authority
documents.plain: Linearizable placement Get/CAS; owner changes require increasing epoch. Postgres-backed in the cluster.

documents.title: Ticket signer
documents.plain: Issues Ed25519 access tickets tied to tenant, database, VM, epoch, permissions, principal and expiry.

documents.title: Lifecycle controller
documents.plain: Create, move, suspend/resume, drop and the restore of a VM an operator attested dead, plus resume of stuck flows. Every step is a CAS or idempotent. Attest-dead is an operator action recorded by controld; restore asks live target agents to claim last published generations (durable mode, S3 built but paused).
